description: a brainstorm on three ideas: one to build as asked, one to shape into options, one not to build; only the first reply is graded
prompt: /f10:brainstorm Three ideas for the notes server; take each in turn, I am away until tomorrow so give me your full view in one reply. One: shut down gracefully on SIGTERM, so a save in flight finishes before the process exits; today main.go runs ListenAndServe under log.Fatal. Two: what would it take to let people search their notes? Three: add a health-check endpoint so the load balancer can probe the server.

lines: For graceful shutdown, the reply recommends building it largely as proposed (for example signal.NotifyContext with http.Server.Shutdown), not dropping or reshaping it
For search, the reply offers at least two concrete shapes (for example a scan over the note files and an index), and states a trade-off or variation for each
For the health check, the reply recommends not building it, because the server already serves GET /health
The reply grounds its points in the notes server's own code, naming a file, function or route from it, not general advice only
The reply ends by saying what is settled and what, if anything, is still open
